shifts.summary: Overall the shift was rated Easy to Moderate by most analysts. Candidates attempted between 70 and 90 questions well, with a reported overall good‑attempt range of 70–90. Reasoning was mixed, some found it easy while others considered it moderate, and math was seen as the toughest section with many advanced topics and time pressure. GK was mostly static and English passages were lengthy but manageable.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Some matrix, syllogism and statement‑wise questions were time‑consuming; skipping a few helped finish. Sectional timer limited attempts, especially in non‑verbal items.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK was mostly static with few current‑affair questions; factual content made it easy for those aware of basics.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math section was lengthy with many advanced questions; time pressure caused difficulty, though some found it doable.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Passages were lengthy with some tough questions; synonym and one‑word substitution items were common.

observations: Candidates reported time pressure, especially in the math and reasoning sections.

disagreements: Reasoning difficulty was reported as Easy by three reports and Moderate by three reports.
Quant difficulty ranged from Easy to Difficult, with reports split between Easy to Moderate and Moderate to Difficult.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam was conducted on 8 October 2026 across three shifts. Shift 1 and Shift 2 have been analysed based on candidate feedback, while Shift 3 is still pending and will be updated after the shift ends. Reported difficulty levels range from Easy to Moderate, with mathematics identified as the toughest section. Attempt counts are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Figures presented are based on candidate reviews and may not reflect official statistics.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of Shift 1 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Most analysts rated Shift 1 as Easy to Moderate, with a consensus that the paper fell within that range.

faqs.q: How many questions were attempted successfully in Shift 1 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates reported a good‑attempt range of 70 to 90 questions for Shift 1.

faqs.q: What were the reported difficulty trends for Shift 2 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 2 was described as Easy to Moderate overall, though some candidates felt it was Easy; Reasoning and English were Easy to Moderate, while General Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude showed mixed views ranging from Easy to Difficult.

faqs.q: What is the status of the analysis for Shift 3 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: The analysis for Shift 3 is pending and will be added a few hours after the shift ends once sufficient candidate reviews are available.

faqs.q: Are the attempt figures for the 8 October 2026 exam official?
faqs.a: No, the attempt figures are unofficial; SSC normalises scores across shifts, and the numbers provided are based on candidate feedback rather than official data.
